Subject: Pricing exception request — HelioHealth pilot structuring

Team,

Quick summary from the call with HelioHealth (Anna / Dan) this morning — they want to accelerate an enterprise pilot that will become a production deployment if performance + cost targets are met. Key asks:

- 18-month pilot with a commit to 8 TB of embeddings + 1.2B generation tokens (estimated first-year consumption).
- Requesting a first-year effective discount that brings list to ~40% off list at the volume tier break; they framed this as necessary to get internal procurement and clinical risk-compliance signoff.
- Asking for a packaged onboarding credit (~$50k) and extended payment net-60 terms for the pilot phase.

Attached: helio_moa_v2.pdf (redlined SOW + mutual action plan). DocuSign link included in related_links.

Why this matters: HelioHealth is a strategic payer in the telehealth vertical — win here helps our marketplace credibility (they want case study rights after pilot) and they have references into three other hospital systems. Upside is meaningful, but the unit economics at a 40% list discount is tight for Hosted without prepayment or committed reserved capacity.

Ask: I need an internal pricing exception / carveout approved to present a concrete number back to Anna today. Recommendation I discussed with the account: offer a structured carveout — 30% off list in year one if they commit to 18-month reserved capacity with a 9-month prepayment for the first tranche; include the $50k onboarding credit as a one-time offset. If Finance signs off on the margin impact, I’d like VP/CFO email signoff (Marissa/Markus) so I can close the loop with procurement today.

If you want numbers to review I can pull updated ARR/GM impact, but we’ll need a quick yes/no for a negotiated concession.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: helio_moa_v2.pdf (SOW redlines, 8 pages)

Camila / Marissa —

I ran the preliminary impact model (attached: financial_impact_twilight.xlsx). High-level:

- Scenario A (recommended): 30% off list, 18-month reserved commitment, 9-month prepayment for the first tranche. Projected first-year gross margin hit: ~18% points vs baseline; NPV over 3 years still positive given expected upsell into production.
- Scenario B: 35% off + 6-month prepay — GM hit ~22% points; acceptable if we get a binding commitment to add 40% incremental capacity in year two.
- Scenario C: 40% off + onboarding credit $50k + no prepay — GM hit ~28% points; this requires either a higher purchase floor or explicit marketing/private case study commitments to justify.

Risks & mitigations:
- If we accept 40% with no prepay we need a security on the commitment (SLA/exit ramp) and an explicit clawback if production conversion doesn't occur by month 12.
- Recommend tying the concession to a reserved SKU that allows us to failover to Dedicated pricing if usage patterns become heavy (protective cap on peak spend).

Recommendation summary: Finance supports Scenario A (30% with 9-month prepay) subject to VP signoff (Marissa) and CFO concurrence (Markus) for the structured carveout language. With those approvals we should provide HelioHealth the letter template for signatures and the DocuSign envelope.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Finance
